name: Great Mosque of Cordoba
_about: THE GREAT MOSQUE OF CORDOBA as it stood in 988, after al-Mansur's extension and before any Christian work: the walled court with its galleries, orange trees and palms and Abd al-Rahman III's minaret; the prayer hall of 19 aisles and 36 bays on some 600 columns, its two-tier arcades of red-and-white horseshoe arches; al-Hakam II's Villaviciosa dome and maqsura of polylobed interlaced arches under three ribbed domes; the octagonal mihrab; the gates in their alfiz frames. Built by tools/archgen/cordoba.py from the components of tools/archgen/andalusi.py (its docstring: what is sourced, what is estimated, what is left out). +z is toward the qibla (south-south-east).

arcades hall 36._about: the hall's arcades: 18 lines of columns, the two tiers of arches over them

arcades maqsura 3 inner._about: al-Hakam II's arcades round the Villaviciosa bay and the maqsura: polylobed arches, interlaced over them

maqsura screen 4._about: a screen of polylobed interlaced arches across the aisle

villaviciosa front 5._about: a screen of polylobed interlaced arches across the aisle

villaviciosa back 5._about: a screen of polylobed interlaced arches across the aisle

villaviciosa lantern._about: the Villaviciosa bay's dome on its lantern: al-Hakam II's threshold, where his hall began (7.85 x 9.45 m)

maqsura lantern 4._about: the maqsura's three domes, the middle one before the mihrab

ceiling._about: the flat ceilings, carved and painted pine, between the arcades' walls

aisle roofs 1._about: a gable roof over every aisle, the gutters between them on the arcades

hall._about: the hall's air, up to the ceilings

west wall._about: the outer walls, ashlar in stretchers and headers, 11 m to the merlons

west merlons._about: the stepped merlons along the top

buttresses x._about: the buttresses, square-headed, against the walls' outside

gate 14._about: the north gate by the minaret

hall front._about: the hall's front to the court, Abd al-Rahman III's: an open horseshoe arch at the head of every aisle

mihrab chamber._about: the mihrab: a small octagonal room behind the qibla wall (3.8 m across inside), entered through the horseshoe arch and a narrower one in its own wall

mihrab shell._about: its dome, a scallop shell cut from one block of marble

mihrab._about: the mihrab's front on the qibla wall: the horseshoe arch in its alfiz, the blind arcade over it -- all in gold mosaic, the Byzantine emperor's gift

west gallery._about: the court's galleries (Abd al-Rahman III's, 951-58): horseshoe arches on columns

west gallery roof._about: the galleries' roofs, falling from the walls to the court

minaret._about: Abd al-Rahman III's minaret (951-58), 8.5 m square, 47 m to the yamur: the model of every Andalusi and Maghrebi minaret after it

orange trunks._about: the court's orange trees, in rows on the aisles' axes

palm trunks._about: and date palms among them (the court's palms are on Cordoba's seals of 1262 and 1445)

palm fronds._about: their crowns of fronds, arching out and down

basins._about: the ablution basins (al-Mansur's cistern under the court fed them)

floor._about: the floor: the hall's and the court's, one level
